### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**22** anchor(s) derived from **3** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-core/src/index.ts`, `packages/metadata-core/src/testing.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-core/src/index.ts`, `packages/metadata-core/src/testing.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **17** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 49aba82b3acf7c3f2810d58698a589d69d510199` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8af54071f293ab3b406950f5b706164390df9841` — the merge of head `8a3843273e8e0485234f3bc85fb16fca5f6b0a81` into base `49aba82b3acf7c3f2810d58698a589d69d510199`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8af54071f293ab3b406950f5b706164390df9841 && git checkout 8af54071f293ab3b406950f5b706164390df9841
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 49aba82b3acf7c3f2810d58698a589d69d510199 8a3843273e8e0485234f3bc85fb16fca5f6b0a81 && git checkout -B drift-repro 49aba82b3acf7c3f2810d58698a589d69d510199 && git merge --no-ff 8a3843273e8e0485234f3bc85fb16fca5f6b0a81

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 49aba82b3acf7c3f2810d58698a589d69d510199
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8a3843273e8e0485234f3bc85fb16fca5f6b0a81`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata-core/src/flow-cycle.ts, packages/metadata-core/src/flow-cycle-corpus.ts, packages/metadata-core/src/index.ts, packages/metadata-core/src/testing.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/runtime-authoring-gate.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-registration-checks.ts, packages/metadata-core/src/flow-cycle.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/runtime-authoring-gate.flow-cycle.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.draft-publish-verdict.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-cycle-registration.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/flow-undeclared-cycle-publish.dogfood.test.ts + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-authoring-gate.ts (`judgeRuntimeAuthoringRules`, `runAuthoringGate`, `draftPublishVerdict`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts (the save door around the flow canonicalizer fallback and the gate, the per-item promotion, the draft read's `serveDraft`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/metadata-diagnostics.ts (`itemRelativeIssuePath`, `withPublishVerdict`), packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-definitions.ts (`canonicalizeFlow`), packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts (`detectCycles` wrapper), packages/spec/src/automation/flow.zod.ts (`FlowEdgeSchema.type`, the edge aliases), packages/spec/src/shared/strict-object.ts (alias semantics), packages/metadata-core/package.json and packages/metadata-protocol/package.json (`exports`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts, .changeset/29025-flow-undeclared-cycle-publish.md (declaration lines and level, read for ②), the merge-base copy of flow-registration-checks.ts (the old walk).

Face: narrowing (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body and the changeset; no published schema under `packages/spec/src/**` and no governed rules text in the tree). Every non-prose path of the diff is in scope above.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept set of the runtime authoring gate narrowed** (`@objectstack/metadata-protocol`): a `flow` body whose top-level `nodes`/`edges` graph, minus every edge with `type: 'back'`, has a cycle is now an `error` finding (`rule: 'flow-undeclared-cycle'`, `path: flows[0].edges[N]` on the cycle-closing edge, `message` = the engine's registration sentence). Severity `error` folds into `localIssues`, so the verdict is the gate's existing `422 INVALID_METADATA`. **Right**, and it is the one accept-set change in the diff.
2. **Which doors it reaches**: the gate's error is thrown by `assertRuntimeAuthoringRules` at (a) the live save door `PUT /api/v1/meta/:type/:name` in non-draft mode (protocol.ts, after the schema gate, before step 1 writes anything), (b) the per-item promotion `POST …/publish` (judged on `draftForGate.body` before `repo.promoteDraft`), (c) `publish-drafts`, which promotes each draft through (b) with `pending` threaded and answers `outcome: 'refused'`, and (d) `duplicatePackage`, whose copies go through the save door by design ("a copy of a broken flow is a new broken flow", protocol-authoring-gate.ts). **Right**; (d) is a consequence the PR text does not name: duplicating a package that holds a stored cyclic flow now refuses the duplicate. By the existing comment's intent, correct.
3. **Draft read**: `serveDraft` runs `draftPublishVerdict` on `storedRowDocument(row)`, and `itemRelativeIssuePath` re-spells `flows[0].edges[4]` to `edges.4`, so `_diagnostics` reads `valid:false` with `code: 'flow-undeclared-cycle'` on `edges.N`. **Right** (the dogfood case pins exactly that spelling).
4. **Draft save unchanged**: `evaluateRuntimeAuthoringGate` returns `{ error: null, advisories: hierarchyScopeGaps }` for `state !== 'active'` above the new call, and `judgeRuntimeAuthoringRules` returns advisories only for a draft. A work-in-progress cycle still saves (D1). **Right**.
5. **`migrate-stored` carve-out unchanged**: the wrapper returns `clean` before the gate for that source, so `os migrate meta --stored` can still heal a stored cyclic row; the active read carries no verdict (unchanged); the engine's registration of a stored cyclic flow is refused exactly as before. **Right**; the changeset's "Unchanged" and "The remedy" bullets state this correctly.
6. **The walk is the engine's, verdict for verdict.** Old `detectCycles` body (merge-base `4550091a1d`) vs `findUndeclaredFlowCycle`: identical adjacency build (`type === 'back'` skipped, edges with an unknown source dropped, an unknown target pushed but never coloured so never GRAY), identical white/gray/black DFS and identical cycle reconstruction, identical outer loop in node declaration order (`if (color !== WHITE) continue` is the old nested `if`), and the same message template. The only edits are the return of `{ path, closingEdgeIndex, message }` in place of `throw`, and the input type widened from `FlowParsed` to a structural slice. `detectCycles` now throws `cycle.message` at the same site in `canonicalizeFlow` (parse → `detectCycles` → `validateControlFlow`, unchanged). **Right**: the engine's verdict and sentence are preserved.
7. **The gate judges the same graph the engine judges.** The engine sees the Zod-parsed flow (edge `type` defaulted to `'default'`); the gate sees the raw body, or the D2-converted raw body when the canonicalizer throws (which it does on a cycle, so this is the path that matters). An absent `type` is `!== 'back'` either way; D2 conversions do not rewrite edge endpoints; node and edge order survive parsing. I checked the one divergence I could think of, the `from`/`to`/`sourceid`/`targetid` edge aliases in `FlowEdgeSchema`: `strictObject` aliases run only from the `unrecognized_keys` path as a suggestion, never a rename, so such an edge is refused by the schema gate upstream of this rule and by `FlowSchema.parse` at registration alike. No graph reaches one judge and not the other. **Right**.
8. **`closingEdgeIndex`** is the first non-`back` edge `from → to` in body order, and `findFlowCycleGaps` maps the body's edges index-preservingly (a member without string endpoints becomes a `back`-typed placeholder, so it takes no part and shifts nothing). With duplicate parallel edges the first untyped one is named, which is the one to mark. **Right**.
9. **Public surface, `@objectstack/metadata-core` root** (`exports["."]`): `findUndeclaredFlowCycle`, `undeclaredFlowCycleMessage`, types `FlowCycleNode`, `FlowCycleEdge`, `FlowUndeclaredCycle`. `./testing` (import-only condition, pre-existing): `FLOW_CYCLE_CORPUS`, `FlowCycleCorpusCase`. Additive; no baseline or ledger lists this package's exports. **Right**.
10. **Public surface, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`**: `FLOW_UNDECLARED_CYCLE` and `findFlowCycleGaps` are module exports of `runtime-authoring-gate.ts`, which `src/index.ts` re-exports only `SDUI_MANIFEST_SERVICE` from, and the package's `exports` map has `"."` alone. They are **not** on the package's public surface; the dev report's open question 2 overstates this. The one new wire value is the rule id string `flow-undeclared-cycle` in `issues[].rule` / `_diagnostics.errors[].code`, plus its presence in `rulesRun` for every flow (ahead of `platform-schedule-create-record-org-missing`; the only pins on that array are `toContain`). **Right** as shipped; the report's wording is corrected here.
11. **`@objectstack/service-automation`**: `detectCycles(flow: FlowParsed): void` keeps its signature, message and throw site; the new `import { findUndeclaredFlowCycle } from '@objectstack/metadata-core'` adds no package edge (five source files on `main` already import that package, and it is in `dependencies`). **Right**; `patch` is the correct level for it.
12. **`hint` text** is gate-only (the engine has none); `message` is byte-identical at both doors. **Right**.

### ② Semver level

- PR body and changeset both carry, line-initial, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`; the changeset heads with a **BREAKING** banner, carries Before / Now / Unchanged bullets and a remedy paragraph, and exactly one `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker. `Check Changeset` and `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` (which runs `check-adr-0087-registration` and `check-changeset-no-major`) are green on this head.
- Levels: `metadata-protocol` **minor**, `metadata-core` **minor**, `service-automation` **patch**.
- The dispatch order framed this as a non-protocol narrowing (ruling A: `patch` with the BREAKING banner and the marker). I judged the kind on AGENTS.md's own words: "a value refused or a requirement tightened is `narrowed`". A flow body the spec accepts and the draft stores is now refused at every publish door, and an author with such a draft must act (the ruling's 需手动处理 group), so `narrowed` is the better reading. Precedent on the same gate is the same: #28448 (save-door rule-copy refusal) and #27968 shipped `narrowed` / `minor`; only the CLI twin #28893 chose `none` / `patch`. Under the ruling the level follows the kind, so `metadata-protocol: minor` is **right**, and the declarations and level agree with each other and with the gates.
- `metadata-core: minor` is the one soft spot: on its own that package only gains exports (ruling A row ④, `patch`); the gate requires at least one moved package at `minor`, which `metadata-protocol` already supplies. Under the fixed version group this changes nothing shipped. **Should-fix, optional** (`patch` would be the tighter reading); not a must-fix.
- `service-automation: patch` **right** (behaviour and surface unchanged).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Open question 1 (gate-local vs `AUTHORING_RULES`)**: **A, as the dev recommends.** `@objectstack/lint` reaches `spec`, `formula` and `sdui-parser` only; a `lint → metadata-core` edge or moving the judge into `packages/spec` is a lane-wide choice and the second is the spec lane's. The gate already hosts gate-local rules (#6155, #21476, #26188, #28448), and the docblock states honestly that this one's reason differs from its neighbours' (a shared judge, not a deployment fact). #29051 (`os validate` / `os build`) stays a separate one-file call on the same judge, as the PR's acceptance note says.
- **Open question 2 (new public names)**: for the maintainer's word before landing, as the dev asks. The rule id `flow-undeclared-cycle` follows the gate's kebab-case ids and is the only new wire value; the `metadata-core` root exports follow the shared-judge pattern (`extension-field-patch-targets`). Correction to the report: `FLOW_UNDECLARED_CYCLE` and `findFlowCycleGaps` are not package-public (①.10). I see no reason to rename; the maintainer's word is the record of that.
- **Dev deviation, changeset banner shape** (Before / Now bullets plus a remedy paragraph instead of a FROM → TO label): the gate reads a FROM → TO label beside `not-required` as a migration prescription, and the chosen shape is the one #25579 landed with. Accepted.
- **Unnamed consequence**: `duplicatePackage` of a package holding a stored cyclic flow now refuses the duplicate (①.2 d). By the existing comment's intent; no change asked. The seat may want it in the PR body's risk line.
- **Out-of-scope finding (class a, region cycles)**: a `loop` / `parallel` / `try_catch` region that `validateControlFlow` refuses still passes the gate and publishes, then never registers. Confirmed from `canonicalizeFlow` (parse → `detectCycles` → `validateControlFlow`) and the gate (no `validateControlFlow` call). Not this card; **escalated to the seat** to file a card as the gate-side twin of #28893, beside #29051.
- **Check-runs on this head at the time of this record** (47 runs): every completed run is `success` or `skipped`; `Build Core`, the eight `Test Core` shards and two `Type Check` runs (workspace, consumer gates) were still `in_progress`. This record judges the tree and the completed conclusions; the all-green landing precondition is the seat's to read before queueing.
- PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no relay author to name.

### ④ Design judgment

- **packages/metadata-core/src/flow-cycle.ts** — holds. One judge, the engine's walk unedited in substance (①.6), pure, `spec`-only package so both faces can depend on it without pulling each other's code. Tried to break it: a self-loop (`again → again`) is found as `['again','again']` with the closing edge the self-edge; an edge typed `fault` or `conditional` still closes a cycle (only `'back'` is set aside, as ADR-0044 and the engine say); any single `back` edge on the loop breaks it (the corpus's `cyc_mid_back`), which is the engine's semantics and not a new one; a dangling endpoint takes no part, as before. The carried-over `parent.get(cur)!; if (cur) … else break` guard is the engine's and is unreachable for a GRAY neighbour on the DFS stack; left as is, correctly, since "unedited" was the contract.
- **packages/metadata-core/src/flow-cycle-corpus.ts** — holds as the parity pin: eight `FlowSchema`-shaped bodies (`start` / `assignment` / `end` only, no conditions, so no other registration or gate rule speaks), four refused / four accepted, the card's shape among them, and the judge's own suite asserts both verdicts are present and names are unique so neither face can pass it by refusing everything or nothing.
- **packages/metadata-core/src/index.ts, testing.ts** — hold: additive barrels on the root and the test-only subpath; the corpus is kept off the runtime entry.
- **packages/metadata-protocol/src/runtime-authoring-gate.ts** — holds against the scenario it is accepted against. Pure (reads the body only); tolerant of a raw body (missing or non-array `nodes` / `edges` read as none, so a schema-refused member is the schema's to report); the closing edge is located by the body's own index (①.8) and the finding is folded into the gate's one verdict and disclosed in `rulesRun`. Drafts are not gated (①.4). The placement before `scheduleOrgGaps` in `localIssues` changes only ordering among gate-local errors, which nothing pins. The docblock's "why gate-local" matches what I read in `@objectstack/lint`'s reach.
- **packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-registration-checks.ts** — holds: same sentence, same throw, same position in `canonicalizeFlow`; `AutomationEngine.detectCycles` still delegates to it. Engine registration is unchanged in verdict and in words.
- **The narrowing itself against the live doors** (the face's own question): at the live save door the canonicalizer throws on a cycle, the gate then judges the D2-converted raw body and throws before step 1 writes (and the fallback warning is said only after acceptance, so no "was saved" log is emitted for a refused body); the per-item promotion judges the stored draft body before `promoteDraft`; `publish-drafts` goes through that promotion with the batch's `pending`, so the batch is refused and `publishedCount` is 0; the draft read says `valid:false` with the located code and the engine's sentence. A loop with any edge typed `back` is unchanged at every door and registers (corpus + draft-verdict control + dogfood control, the last of which waits for `registration.state: registered`). Stored flows: the active read is unchanged, registration is unchanged, `migrate-stored` is not gated; a re-save as active of such a row is now refused with the remedy, which is the narrowing. **The narrowing makes the engine's own refusal real one door earlier and takes no registrable capability away.**
- **Test files** (read for the parity claim, not reviewed): the three corpus-driven suites assert the same set of refusals on the judge, `registerFlow` and the pure gate with the judge's message; the draft-verdict table gains the card's push → check → revise → push row with `conditional` edges on the decision, kept last so #26707's six keep their positions; the dogfood case drives both doors over REST on the showcase composition.
- No must-fix found. Should-fix: `metadata-core` at `patch` (②); the report's "metadata-protocol exports" wording (①.10) needs no code change.
